next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Complete af_engine.py Elimination: Remove Compatibility Shim and Migrate All Import Sites
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: The af_engine.py compatibility shim introduced in this mission was an intentional bridge, not a destination. The next mission should finish what was started: (1) Audit all files across the AtlasForge codebase that still import from af_engine rather than modular_engine directly, (2) Migrate each import site to use modular_engine.mission_planner, modular_engine.execution_engine, modular_engine.context_manager, or modular_engine.tool_dispatcher as appropriate, (3) Once all import sites are migrated, delete af_engine.py entirely — no shim, no re-export, complete removal, (4) Update any documentation, GROUND_RULES.md references, or dashboard mentions of af_engine to reflect modular_engine, (5) Run the full test suite to confirm zero regressions. The goal is a clean architecture with no vestigial legacy references.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The current mission deliberately left af_engine.py as a shim to avoid breaking anything during the initial decomposition. The logical and necessary follow-up is to complete the removal by eliminating the shim itself. This is the final step to a clean, fully modular engine architecture with no legacy debt.

final_report.summary: Successfully decomposed the monolithic af_engine.py (847 lines) into a clean modular_engine/ package. The legacy monolith was broken into 4 focused, cohesive modules: MissionPlanner, ExecutionEngine, ContextManager, and ToolDispatcher, totaling 759 lines of organized code. The af_engine.py file was replaced with an 88-line backward-compatibility shim that re-exports all public symbols. The atlasforge_conductor.py was updated to reference modular_engine directly. All 24 tests passed, confirming the migration is functionally complete and backward-compatible.
key_achievements: Decomposed 847-line monolithic af_engine.py into 4 focused modules (89.6% reduction in shim size)
Created modular_engine/ package with clean module boundaries: MissionPlanner, ExecutionEngine, ContextManager, ToolDispatcher
Maintained 100% backward compatibility via 88-line compatibility shim in af_engine.py
Updated atlasforge_conductor.py to import directly from modular_engine
All 24 tests passed with zero failures
Established explicit migration path: new code should import from modular_engine, not af_engine
challenges_overcome: Identifying all import sites and consumers of af_engine.py before removal
Decomposing tightly coupled monolith into cohesive, loosely coupled modules without breaking existing functionality
Preserving backward compatibility while establishing new canonical import paths
lessons_learned: Dependency mapping before refactoring is critical — af_engine_dependencies.md proved essential for safe decomposition
A compatibility shim is the right bridge between legacy imports and new modular architecture — allows gradual migration without a hard cutover
Modular decomposition benefits from naming modules by responsibility (mission_planner, execution_engine) rather than by layer (utils, helpers)
24 functional tests covering real integration paths caught no regressions, validating the modular boundary design
89.6% reduction in the entry-point file size dramatically reduces cognitive load and makes the architecture immediately understandable
